Destination can be a directory or file name. If destination is a directory, source will be copied into that directory. But we want rename. We can use mv to rename within same directory? But we want to copy to archive folder. We can use cp to copy to archive folder, then mv to rename? But cp cannot specify path. We can first cp to archive folder: cp source: "project_summary.txt" destination: "archive". That will copy into archive folder with same name. Then mv source: "archive/project_summary.txt" destination: "archive/summary_2024.txt"? But mv also requires source local to current directory. So cannot specify path. So we can copy to archive folder, then rename inside archive folder. But mv cannot specify path. So we cannot rename inside archive folder. So maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder, then use mv to rename the file in archive folder? But mv cannot specify path. So we cannot rename inside archive folder. So maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder, then use mv to rename the file in current directory? But we want to rename the copy, not the original. So we cannot rename the copy because mv cannot specify path. So we might need to use cp to copy to archive folder, then use mv to rename the original file to summary_2024.txt? But that would lose original. So maybe we can use cp to copy to archive folder, then use mv to rename the copy inside archive folder by moving it to a new name in current directory?
